data.title: NexGold Reminds Warrant Holders of Upcoming Expiry
data.description:
Not for Distribution to U.S. Newswire Services or Dissemination in the United States

TORONTO, Oct. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NexGold Mining Corp. (TSXV: NEXG; OTCQX: NXGCF) (“NexGold” or the “Company”) reminds holders of its common share purchase warrants issued pursuant to the Company’s flow-through private placement completed on November 6, 2024 (the “Warrants”) that the Warrants will expire at 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on Friday, November 6, 2026 (the “Expiry Date”).

Each Warrant entitles the holder to acquire one common share of the Company at an exercise price of $1.05 until the Expiry Date. The original financing terms disclosed by the Company provided for a 24-month exercise period from November 6, 2024.

As of October 8, 2026, 1,211,250 Warrants remain outstanding. Any Warrants not exercised in accordance with their terms by 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on the Expiry Date will expire and cease to be exercisable.

Holders wishing to exercise their Warrants should ensure that all required exercise documentation and funds are delivered in accordance with the terms of the Warrants sufficiently in advance of the Expiry Date. Beneficial holders whose Warrants are held through a broker, investment dealer or other intermediary should promptly contact their intermediary regarding the applicable exercise procedures and any deadlines imposed by the intermediary, which may be earlier than the Expiry Date.

The Warrants and the common shares issuable upon exercise thereof have not been, and will not be, registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “U.S. Securities Act”), or any applicable U.S. state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration under the U.S. Securities Act and applicable U.S. state securities laws or an available exemption therefrom. This news release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy any securities.

The Warrants are governed by the terms of the applicable warrant certificates and related transaction documents. In the event of any inconsistency between this news release and such documents, the terms of the applicable warrant certificates and related transaction documents will govern.

For More Information

Questions regarding the exercise of Warrants should be directed to the holder’s broker or other intermediary, as applicable. General questions may be directed to the Company at ir@nexgold.com.

Sprott Royalty – Shares For Debt Issuance

Pursuant to the terms of a royalty agreement with Sprott Resources Streaming and Royalty Corp. (“Sprott Streaming”) announced on February 14, 2022 and amended on May 1, 2024 (the “Royalty Agreement”), the Company has elected to satisfy an upcoming minimum payment of US$675,000 due under the Royalty Agreement through the issuance of 716,619 common shares of the Company (the “Common Shares”) to Sprott Streaming (“Common Shares”) at a deemed price of $1.3427 per Common Share.

Under the Royalty Agreement, NexGold is required to make minimum payments of US$675,000 on a quarterly basis, payable, at the Company’s election, in cash or Common Shares. The Common Shares are proposed to be issued as shares for debt in accordance with Policy 4.3 of the TSX Venture Exchange (“TSXV”) Corporate Finance Policies. The issuance of the Common Shares has been approved by the Board of Directors of NexGold and remains subject to the acceptance of the TSXV. Subject to receipt of such acceptance, NexGold expects to issue the Common Shares to Sprott Streaming on or about October 13, 2026.

About NexGold Mining Corp.

NexGold is a gold-focused company with assets in Canada and Alaska, including the Goldboro Gold Project in Nova Scotia, the Goliath Gold Complex (which includes the Goliath, Goldlund and Miller deposits) in Northwestern Ontario, and additional exploration projects across Canada. NexGold also holds a 100% interest in the high-grade Niblack copper-gold-zinc-silver VMS project in southeast Alaska. NexGold is committed to ongoing, meaningful engagement with regional communities and Indigenous Nations to support sustainable development, safe operations, and shared economic and social benefits.

Further details about NexGold, including a Feasibility Study for the Goldboro Gold Project and a Prefeasibility Study for the Goliath Gold Complex, are available under the Company’s issuer profile on www.sedarplus.ca and on NexGold’s website at www.nexgold.com

data.title: Gran Tierra Energy expects $315M cash from $1.33B business sale
data.description:
Gran Tierra Energy announced on Friday that stockholders approved the sale of its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses to Maurel & Prom for approximately $1.33B.

The company expects to receive ~$315M in net cash proceeds, including $250M at closing and $65M payable 364 days later.

The deal still requires regulatory approvals in Colombia and Ecuador, with closing targeted for December 31, 2026.

Moreover, it expects to be debt-free after the sale and plans to use part of the proceeds for a share repurchase, subject to completion of the sale and board approval.

On the market side, the GTE stock traded ~3% higher at ~$10.90 in the after-hours session.

data.title: Qualcomm and Arm jury to return next week after deliberations in contract dispute case
data.description:
Key points:
  • Qualcomm asks jury to find Arm intentionally interfered with Meta dealings by leaking 2024 breach letter
  • Qualcomm says Arm withheld software patches and design tools in breach of licensing agreements
  • Judge has not ruled on Qualcomm claim it could stop paying royalties for five years

By Tom Hals and Stephen Nellis

The jury in a lawsuit by chipmaker Qualcomm against chip technology supplier Arm Holdings did not reach a verdict on Friday as to whether Arm breached licensing agreements and intentionally sabotaged some of Qualcomm's dealings with Meta Platforms .

The five-day trial that wrapped up this week was the second in two years between the companies, highlighting the deterioration of their business relationship after SoftBank Group acquired control of Arm in 2016 and Arm shifted from licensing the technology needed to make chips to selling chips of its own.

At stake is whether Qualcomm, whose license for Arm's computing architecture runs until 2033, can eventually agree to terms for new versions of Arm's architecture.

After deliberating for about four hours Friday, the jury had not reached a verdict, indicating it would return to deliberations on Tuesday.

Qualcomm wants the jury to find that Arm breached its licensing agreements by withholding software patches and tools for its designs and by violating an agreement that was meant to ensure Qualcomm paid within 10% of the lowest price for Arm's processor designs.

It also wants the jury to find that Arm tried to torpedo Qualcomm's dealings with Meta by leaking to Bloomberg an Arm letter in 2024 notifying Qualcomm it was allegedly in breach of a key license agreement.

Arm's legal team this week tried to focus the jury on its claim that Qualcomm had not suffered any harm from the allegations in its lawsuit, which Arm cast as an attempt to exert leverage as the two fought over licensing terms. A related bench trial also took place this week over whether Arm is negotiating in good faith over those terms, though a decision on that could come well after Friday's verdict.

The trial in Wilmington, Delaware, federal court hinged on many of the same episodes as the 2024 trial in which Arm failed to convince a jury that Qualcomm had breached its licensing agreement with Arm. Both trials included testimony by both Arm CEO Rene Haas and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon and were overseen by US District Judge Maryellen Noreika.

Qualcomm's lawyer Karen Dunn said in her opening statement that the case was very serious for the company.

"It’s really bad because Qualcomm’s entire chip business depends on Arm and on Arm honoring its contract and honoring its promises," she said on Monday.

Qualcomm wanted Noreika to rule prior to trial that a clause in the licensing agreements meant that Qualcomm could stop paying royalties for five years if the contract were breached. She has not issued her ruling, and Arm has argued the royalty penalty is unenforceable.

"They were not harmed in the least," Arm's attorney Gregg LoCascio told the jury on Monday.

data.title: Mexican court finds three men guilty of 2024 killing of Australian, US surfers
data.description:
A Mexican judge on Friday found three men guilty of the 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a surf trip to the state of Baja California, a source at the court told Reuters.

The charges against the defendants include robbery and aggravated homicide, for which the prosecution had sought sentences of up to 150 years against the suspects. The sentence will be announced in the coming days.

data.title: CVS Stock Dips After Drop in Medicare Advantage Plan Ratings — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Catherine Dunn

Shares of CVS Health fell Friday after its insurance arm Aetna lost ground in the latest ratings of Medicare Advantage plans for seniors.

The stock was down 1.2%, while peer Humana, which made big gains in the ratings, was up 12% in late morning trading.

Insurance plans in the federal program are rated each year on a scale of one to five stars, summing up performance on dozens of quality measures. Seniors can view the star ratings as they shop this fall for next year's health coverage.

Wall Street tracks the ratings closely because plans that achieve four stars or more become eligible for bonus payments worth billions of dollars in total. The 2027 ratings will lead to bonuses in 2028, paid on a per-member basis.

The portion of Aetna membership in a four-star or higher plan shrank compared with last year, per the new 2027 ratings released Thursday after the market closed.

According to Aetna, about 69% of its members are in a 2027 plan with at least four stars, down from about 81% when the 2026 stars were first announced.

The ratings "came in weaker than expected" for CVS, said TD Cowen analyst Charles Rhyee in a research note Thursday evening. Rhyee estimated the "unmitigated impact" from lower year-over-year ratings at $720 million in 2028.

"While disappointing, we see potential for CVS to partially offset through benefit design," Rhyee wrote. "We expect additional color on the Stars outcome, mitigation opportunities, and sizable impacts" when CVS reports earnings for the third quarter.

Aetna President Steve Nelson said the insurer was "encouraged by our performance in areas like clinical quality and operational excellence" in the ratings.

Nelson said Aetna has "confidence in our ability to achieve our goal of returning to appropriate margins while at the same time driving continuous improvement and delivering even better experiences and outcomes for the members who count on us."

Raymond James analysts called ratings declines "relatively modest" at both CVS and UnitedHealth Group, and said the drops at both companies "can be largely mitigated through plan diversification by 2028."

UnitedHealth shares were up about 1% Friday morning.

data.title: CFTC Proposes to Expand Definition of Swaps to Include Prediction Markets Trading
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is proposing to provide what it describes as additional clarity on the term "swap" that would include event contracts used in prediction market trading.

The expanded term would encompass event contracts on sporting, political, cultural and weather-related events, the CFTC said in a statement Friday.

The proposal notes that event contracts are financial instruments commonly known to trade as swaps.

The prediction markets industry, which is regulated by the CFTC, has been enmeshed in a debate about whether trading on events constitutes gambling, which would put it under the legal purview of states. The CFTC has said that the emerging industry is a form of financial trading, not betting.

"These products are commodity derivatives squarely within the CFTC's regulatory remit under the Commodity Exchange Act and are within the agency's exclusive jurisdiction," CFTC Chair Michael Selig said.

The agency is seeking public comment on the proposal. Comments must be submitted within 30 days.

data.title: Amazon shuffles Alexa leadership following high-end tablet release
data.description:
By Greg Bensinger

Amazon on Friday confirmed it was shuffling leadership in its Alexa division, a day after the company announced its first tablet computers featuring the voice assistant.

Daniel Rausch, a 17-year Amazon veteran who has served as vice president of Alexa and Echo for over three years, is stepping away from the unit next month, Amazon said in response to a Reuters inquiry.

Rausch, who has served as the face of Alexa at events and global launches, will return in another capacity in the devices and services division in 2027.

In his place, Amazon will install Aidan Marcuss, currently the vice president of Fire TV, advertising and the Amazon appstore. Marcuss joined Amazon from Microsoft in early 2025. He oversaw the release of a new Fire TV stick last month, which has garnered mixed reviews.

Kevin Keith, a product and marketing vice president, will keep that role but also take on Marcuss' responsibilities for the time being, Amazon said. The company declined to provide additional detail about the changes.

Alexa has been a consistent money-loser for Amazon since its release in 2014.

Amazon spent several years developing a new version of the voice assistant offering generative AI that can respond to longer prompts. The service is featured in the new Alexa Tablets announced on Thursday that Amazon has priced as a high-end product compared with prior Fire tablets that were inexpensive.

Alexa+, as the latest version is known, is included in the $139-per-year Prime membership or for $20 monthly as a standalone service.

data.title: White House Names Katie Zacharia as New Press Secretary — WSJ
data.description:
By Brian Schwartz and Philip Wegmann

WASHINGTON — President Trump has appointed Katie Zacharia, a conservative commentator, as the new White House press secretary.

Zacharia currently serves as a communications adviser to Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates the Truth Social platform where Trump frequently posts. She also worked briefly at the Department of Homeland Security earlier in Trump's second term. She has also appeared as a commentator on media outlets including CNN, Fox News and Newsmax.

Trump said in a Truth Social post that Zacharia, a California native, had also been involved in his previous campaigns. "She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," he wrote. "She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!"

Zacharia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

She will succeed Karoline Leavitt, who was one of President Trump's closest advisers. Leavitt, who left the job over the summer, recently announced she would join Fox News as a contributor. Trump on Friday again praised Leavitt, saying she "did a fantastic job."

Trump has had an increasingly contentious relationship with White House reporters, and has attempted to bar some news organizations from the White House. His latest effort — targeting CNN, Politico and MS NOW — has been put on hold by a court for now while the outlets pursue a legal challenge.

The move to name a press secretary comes with just weeks to go until the November election, as Trump attempts to sell voters on his administration's accomplishments and convince them to turn out to support Republican candidates and keep his party in control of Congress.

Write to Brian Schwartz at brian.schwartz@wsj.com and Philip Wegmann at philip.wegmann@wsj.com

data.title: Microsoft is nearing a big milestone that solidifies its revival
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

Microsoft is close to reclaiming a $4 trillion market cap - and fresh records are also in sight

Microsoft is nearing a $4 trillion market cap for the first time since last October.

Microsoft is closing in on $4 trillion territory for the first time in nearly a year, helping to cap a wild ride that's seen the company find its way back into investors' good graces.

Worth $3.97 trillion as of midday Friday, Microsoft (MSFT) is not only on the verge of recapturing a $4 trillion market capitalization but it is also within a hair of its highest-ever market value. Microsoft was last worth $4 trillion on Oct. 29, 2025, and it hit a peak market cap of $4.029 trillion the day before that, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Microsoft is the fourth-largest company in the U.S., behind Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL) and Amazon.com (AMZN).

The round trip since last October encapsulates how Microsoft first fell out of fashion on Wall Street in the face of concerns about its cloud growth and the durability of its software business. Lately, however, investors are seeing those businesses in a fresh light, and Microsoft has re-emerged as a stable software bet at a time when investors are questioning how turbulence at top AI labs could impact the companies that rely on their models and spending.

Shares of Microsoft are up more than 50% from their 2026 low, logged in June.

Microsoft has carved out a niche as a model-agnostic software company, meaning its software offerings aren't tied to one model. It's also sporting a growth story that stands out on Wall Street.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch that the acceleration is a big reason for investors' renewed optimism. The company has seen increasing returns on its AI spending, he said.

As long as Microsoft continues to demonstrate healthy cloud growth, AI returns and adoption of its Copilot assistant, the company is likely to continue on its growth trajectory, StoneX analyst Yi Fu Lee told MarketWatch.

Lee added that Microsoft's hardware event earlier this week, which featured an appearance by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to help show off an AI laptop collaboration, is a prime example of how Microsoft is broadening its AI strategy. At the event, Microsoft touted its Surface laptop, which runs on Nvidia systems and shows how the company is seeking to capitalize on AI beyond just software and the cloud.

More from MarketWatch: Microsoft and Nvidia are teaming up on a supercharged AI laptop

More broadly, investors view the legacy software giant as trustworthy, Argus Research analyst Joseph Bonner told MarketWatch last week.

He said that "corporate America may just have more trust" in Azure and Microsoft's AI harnesses - or the software that enables a large language model to execute tasks and run tools - more "than any of the frontier AI labs."

Shares of Microsoft were up roughly 2% in afternoon action on Friday.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc. Receives Nasdaq Minimum Bid Price Deficiency Notice
data.description:
NANCHANG, China, Oct. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc. (the "Company") today announced that it received a written notice dated October 7, 2026 from Nasdaq stating that the closing bid price of its ordinary shares was below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days, from August 25 through October 6, 2026. Accordingly, the Company does not meet the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2).

Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has 180 calendar days, until April 5, 2027, to regain compliance. Compliance requires a closing bid price of at least $1.00 per share for a minimum of ten consecutive business days during that period, subject to Nasdaq's discretion to require a longer period and its written confirmation.

The notice has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's ordinary shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

About Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc.

Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc. is an AI-driven education technology company focused on intelligent content recognition, automated assessment and next-generation learning systems. The Company has historically developed and provided AI-enabled teaching, learning and assessment solutions, including smart homework, smart examination and digital education services, and since September 2025 has provided campus operations and student-life services through its Smart Campus Services business.

The Company is presenting its group businesses under the Formind Group identity as part of its broader strategy to expand AI education, language learning, institutional education support and global technology initiatives. data.title: Humana Stock Surges After Key Medicare Advantage Plan Gets Higher Rating — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Catherine Dunn

Humana stock gained 11.56% Friday after the federal government released new ratings data on Medicare Advantage plans, showing that Humana increased its membership in four-star rated plans, a key metric closely watched by Wall Street.

Shares ended the session at $431.87, Humana's highest close since Jan. 17, 2024, when they ended the day at $447.76, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

After a sharp fall two years ago, the insurer was looking to make a comeback on the new 2027 ratings, which were anticipated this week. The ratings are tied to financial bonuses in the Medicare Advantage program, and Humana's results were expected to test the stock, which had already soared this year. It's now up more than 68% year to date, versus 14% for the broader market.

Humana made big strides in the latest ratings round. The company said 95% of its members are now enrolled in plans rated four stars or higher, up from 45% earlier this year.

In a securities filing Friday morning, Humana said it is "well positioned to deliver on its commitment of unlocking the earnings potential of the business by 2028."

"Bottom Line: HUM...is the clearest positive big winner in our 2027 Stars analysis," Leerink Partners said in a client note.

As seniors begin to shop for Medicare health coverage this month, the rating system is meant to help them compare the quality of plans, on a scale of one to five stars.

For insurers and Wall Street, star ratings are an incredibly important metric because they determine quality bonus payments to insurers from the government. Plans rated four stars and above are eligible for the bonuses. This year alone, those bonus payments are expected to total more than $13 billion in aggregate.

At Humana, "getting the quality bonus payment back on some of their large contracts is empirical to the margin recovery story," Leerink Partners analyst Whit Mayo told Barron's in an interview this week. "That's the primary investment thesis for investors."

The challenge for Humana started two years ago, when the insurer saw a ratings drop, and went from having more than 90% of its members in a plan rated at least four stars, down to about 25%. At the time, Humana said it had narrowly missed thresholds on a small number of measures used to calculate stars. That reduction impacted Humana's ability to collect bonuses this year.

When the 2026 ratings were announced last year, the results continued to show a gap between Humana and industry peers CVS Health and UnitedHealth Group, each with more than 80% of their members in plans with four or more stars this year, according to Leerink.

On Thursday, both CVS Health and UnitedHealth Group saw some decline in that measure for 2027, with about 70% of each company's membership in a four-star or higher plan next year, a Leerink analysis found.

A UnitedHealth spokesperson said the new star ratings "are in line with our expectations and reflect our continued investment in improving members' health outcomes."

CVS Health's Aetna insurance arm, in a statement, said the results position the company as a high performer "for the third consecutive year and highlight strong performance across various clinical quality, preventive care and member experience measures."

CVS shares lost 1.87% Friday, closing at $86.16, while UnitedHealth stock rose 2.25%, for a closing price of $379.30.

Alignment Healthcare, which said Thursday that a California HMO contract received a 3.5-star rating for 2027, tumbled more than 13% Friday, to $7.55 at market close. In a statement, the company said it "believes the rating does not accurately reflect the contract's longstanding performance on evidence-based measures of quality, clinical outcomes and member experience."

Humana was aiming for a boost in 2027 stars, which translate to bonus payments in 2028. Improving the ratings wasn't going to be an overnight fix. Stars are based on 40-some criteria that encompass patient experience surveys and a range of care metrics.

During Humana's last earnings call in July, CEO James Rechtin said he felt good about the company's "operational progress," adding that the company was driven "to be closing every single gap we possibly can..."

The insurer is "very focused on consumer engagement," said Mayo. Efforts to lift ratings are "probably one of the most important initiatives that Humana has had for two years."

A question for Wall Street was just how much the company needed to improve this time around, particularly when it came to one of its largest Medicare Advantage contracts, known as H5216. That contract ultimately moved up to a four-star rating, new data show.

Write to Catherine Dunn at catherine.dunn@dowjones.com

data.title: Lockheed Martin unveils PAC-3 Edge interceptor designed to counter hypersonic threats
data.description:
Lockheed Martin on Friday unveiled PAC-3 Edge, a missile interceptor designed to defend against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the US military looks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats.

Growing demand for air and missile defense systems amid conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East has strained US weapons stockpiles, prompting the US Army to award Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6 billion in July to ramp up production of PAC-3 interceptors.

Lockheed Martin said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls and a multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman, enhancing the interceptor's ability to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic missiles, at longer ranges and higher altitudes.

"The cost of this would be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE," Tim Cahill, president of missiles and fire control at Lockheed Martin, told Reuters. "At full production, the annual rate would be about 2,000 units a year, comparable with PAC-3 MSE."

In January, Lockheed Martin signed a seven-year framework agreement with the US Department of Defense to expand production of its PAC-3 missile interceptors, aiming to increase annual manufacturing capacity to 2,000 units from about 600.
